metadata.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training (Radford et al., 2018)
metadata.framework: Generative pre-training of a left-to-right Transformer language model followed by discriminative fine-tuning on downstream tasks
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of GPT-1 tech report. No arXiv version available.

nodes.name: GPT model architecture
nodes.statement: A 12-layer Transformer decoder (left-to-right, causal attention) with 768-dimensional hidden states, 12 attention heads, and 3072-dimensional feed-forward inner layers. Total ~117M parameters. Uses learned position embeddings and byte-pair encoding (BPE) tokenization.

nodes.name: Generative pre-training objective (left-to-right LM)
nodes.statement: Pre-train by maximizing the left-to-right language modeling likelihood: $L_1(\mathcal{U}) = \sum_i \log P(u_i | u_{i-k}, \ldots, u_{i-1}; \Theta)$ over a large unsupervised corpus $\mathcal{U}$ of tokens, where $k$ is the context window size. Each token attends only to previous tokens (causal masking).

nodes.name: Discriminative fine-tuning
nodes.statement: For each downstream task, add a linear output layer on top of the final Transformer hidden state and fine-tune all parameters. The input is formatted as a single contiguous token sequence with delimiter tokens. Fine-tuning maximizes $L_3 = L_2 + \lambda L_1$ where $L_2$ is the task-specific loss and $\lambda L_1$ is an auxiliary language modeling loss that improves generalization.

nodes.name: Task-specific input transformations
nodes.statement: Different tasks are converted to a single sequence format: Classification: [Start] text [Extract]. Entailment: [Start] premise [Delim] hypothesis [Extract]. Similarity: two orderings concatenated. Multiple choice: context paired with each answer. The [Extract] token's representation is used for prediction.

nodes.name: Left-to-right vs. bidirectional
nodes.statement: GPT uses unidirectional (left-to-right) attention: each token can only attend to tokens at earlier positions. This enables autoregressive generation but means the representation of each token does not incorporate rightward context. This is the key architectural difference from BERT.

nodes.name: Pre-training corpus
nodes.statement: GPT is pre-trained on BooksCorpus (~7000 unpublished books, ~800M words), providing long contiguous text for learning long-range dependencies. BERT later adds English Wikipedia (2500M words).

nodes.name: State-of-the-art on 9 of 12 benchmarks
nodes.statement: GPT achieves state-of-the-art on 9 of 12 evaluated tasks, including commonsense reasoning (Stories Cloze 86.5%), question answering (RACE 59.0%), textual entailment (MultiNLI 82.1%), and GLUE (72.8%). These results are later surpassed by BERT.
